ELI5: What is lucid dreaming and why can we do it?

It's training yourself to realize/notice that you are in a dream. Once you know you're dreaming, you're able to influence what goes on in the dream. I can't tell you "why." It usually takes me more than 10hrs of sleep to really catch on, and not just catch the very end of a dream.

1. Realize you're dreaming.
  2. Have a 3 way with Natalie Portman and Mila Kunis.
  3. ???
  4. Realize that one of the best sexual experiences of your life was all a dream.

But to sort of seriously answer your question, I can only relate why I can do it. For weeks after the movie Westworld came out, I had a recurring nightmare about Yul Brenner chasing through underground tunnels. The first few were terrifying. The next few I began to tell myself it was just a dream. I couldn't do anything about it, but it was less terrifying. Then one night I got out of the tunnel. After that I started getting better at ditching the psycho robot for the fun robots, and that was the end of that recurring dream.

Now I rarely have nightmares, and when I do, I quickly take control. Sometimes I shut it down, sometimes I turn it into an adventure, sometimes I just tweak it a bit. I tend to roll with regular dreams, but I will guide them occasionally...like if I find myself in a cool house with a huge bed and decide I want a 3 way with Mila and Natalie.

I basically achieved lucid dreaming the same way. I had a reoccurring nightmare where I was chased around a house until I made it out, but couldn't run far. One night, I was able to run really fast after getting out of the house, and that kind of opened up lucid dreaming for me. Now, ever dream I have usually have a super power, whether it's teleportation, flight, or telekinesis. Nightmares are usually me defeating the bad guy while normal dreams I just let it take its course.
Yes, but my problem is that I can't move in dreams even if I try. Not that I'd have to move in a Mila+Natalie dream...
The actresses you picked really tell your age.

Lucid dreaming is a dream where you realize you are dreaming. This lets you enjoy the wonder of a dream while it's happening, lets you react to scenarios differently since you know it is a dream, and even control elements of the dream world in ways you couldn't do in real life (flying, jumping into mirrors or paintings, teleporting, summoning things etc.).

There are just two things you will need to practice to start having lucid dreams:

  1. Practice "reality checks." As many times as you can throughout the day, earnestly ask yourself whether you might be dreaming at this very moment- and observe your senses, environment, and situation for something that couldn't possibly be real-life-- proof that you are in a dream. Examine very closely everything available to your perception, expecting some strange or supernatural thing to happen any moment, revealing that you are in a dream. Once you have this built this habit, your dreaming self will automatically start doing it too. And when you do it during a dream you will always discover something fantastical that wouldn't happen in real life, and at that very moment you will become lucid! You're conscious inside your own dream. Now you can try all sorts of things or just play along and see what happens!

  2. Practice "dream recall." Unfortunately, if you don't always remember your dreams, you will not get the full benefit of lucid dreaming. Your dreaming self could be having all sorts of fun with lucid dreams but you wouldn't even know it. Your dreaming self might get skilled at becoming lucid in stressful or frightening situations, and then escaping them, which could actually help you sleep better and have fewer nightmares. But this will all be more fun if you can remember some of these adventures when you wake up. To practice dream recall, keep a dream journal where you write down or record your dreams whenever possible after waking. If you have really good concentration you can also just try to re-live or memorize the experience of your dream for as long as you can after waking. Practicing this will train your brain to store memories while dreaming, and you will be able to remember your lucid dreams as vividly as though they were real experiences.
